themes_detail.label: Illegal Fireworks Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal fireworks complaints spiked to 32 THIS WEEK, a 5020% increase from the 0.6 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 28.24), suggesting either a sudden organized pattern or major enforcement gap during a holiday or event period.
evidence: 32 illegal fireworks complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Z-score of 28.24 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Spike represents 5020% increase in one week
reporting_angles: Investigate whether spike is tied to specific holiday, event, or celebration in Hillcrest/Fresh Meadows
Interview NYPD about enforcement response and whether organized groups are operating in the district
Talk to residents about noise, safety concerns, and impact on sleep/children during spike period

themes_detail.label: Street Condition Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints surged to 204 THIS WEEK, a 514% jump from the 33.2 weekly average (z-score: 19.1), indicating either severe pothole/pavement damage, inadequate snow/ice removal, or a recent weather event that exposed infrastructure failures.
evidence: 204 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 33.2 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Z-score of 19.1 indicates severe statistical anomaly
Street Condition is already #6 complaint type overall (1073 in 90 days), now experiencing crisis-level acceleration
Long-term community board budget request for street reconstruction suggests chronic infrastructure problems
reporting_angles: Canvass streets in Hillcrest/Fresh Meadows to document specific conditions (potholes, flooding, pavement damage)
Contact DOT to ask about recent inspections, repair schedules, and whether weather event triggered complaints
Interview residents about transportation hazards and costs to vehicles; interview small business owners about delivery/operational impact

themes_detail.label: Residential Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Residential noise complaints jumped to 174 THIS WEEK, a 69% increase over the 103.1 weekly average (z-score: 7.36), suggesting either new noise sources, construction activity, or a change in household density/late-night behavior.
evidence: 174 residential noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 103.1 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Z-score of 7.36 indicates high statistical significance
Residential noise is already #4 complaint type overall (1544 in 90 days), suggesting an endemic problem now worsening
517 building permits filed in last 90 days (278 alteration filings) may indicate construction-related noise drivers
reporting_angles: Identify which blocks/neighborhoods within CD408 are generating the surge (map complaints to specific streets)
Investigate whether active construction projects coincide with noise complaints
Interview residents in high-complaint areas about noise sources (parties, music, construction, traffic) and police response times

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Spike
themes_detail.summary: Park noise complaints jumped to 4 THIS WEEK, a 3100% increase from the 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 11.72), suggesting a new activity, event, or facility use triggering complaints in district parks.
evidence: 4 park noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Z-score of 11.72 indicates extreme statistical anomaly despite low absolute numbers
Long-term community board budget requests for park facility upgrades suggest aging infrastructure and underinvestment
reporting_angles: Identify which parks are generating complaints (Fresh Meadows Park, Alley Pond, others)
Investigate what new activities or events are happening (concerts, sports leagues, private rentals)
Talk to Parks Dept. about noise permits, enforcement, and whether event programming has expanded

themes_detail.label: Building/Construction Violations Spike
themes_detail.summary: Building/Use complaints spiked to 29 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 262% increase from the 8.0 weekly average (z-score: 7.31), coinciding with 517 building permits filed in the last 90 days, suggesting inadequate inspector oversight of ongoing construction and alterations.
evidence: 29 Building/Use complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 8.0 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Z-score of 7.31 indicates high statistical significance
517 total DOB filings in last 90 days with 278 alterations suggests active construction environment
Community board has repeated, long-standing budget request to 'Assign additional building inspectors' indicating chronic shortage
reporting_angles: Cross-reference complaint locations with active DOB permits to identify problem construction sites
Interview DOB about inspector capacity and whether staffing is adequate for the 517 permits filed
Talk to residents and neighbors of major construction projects about permit violations, noise, and safety hazards
